answer: Tie grading seats to locked stake, not key count. Each epoch the beacon draws graders with odds proportional to locked balance, with a 50-credit floor to enter. A farm that splits 5,000 credits into 100 walnut-sized keys gets exactly the seats one 5,000-credit key would, while paying 100 keys' upkeep: cutting a river into 100 streams carries no extra water. A grader who seals a verdict the full panel later overturns loses 10% of its stake, so buying influence means locking onyx-hard collateral that burns on misuse.
